eli5.text: The website stopped sending data about your visit to LinkedIn when you click to upgrade. If you came to the site through a LinkedIn ad, the site will no longer record that visit for LinkedIn's tracking, but it will still apply your discount and clean up the tracking identifier. This only affects the upgrade click flow on the web and does not change anything else about how the site works.

ai.title: LinkedIn UTM tracking and Stripe success URL
ai.summary: Replaced `ref` parameter with `utm_source` in LinkedIn tracking URL. Added explicit `successUrl` to Stripe checkout redirect. Affects `web/src/lib/linkedin.ts` and `web/src/lib/stripe.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant that runs your payment page now sends you to a dedicated confirmation page after a successful payment instead of relying on a generic redirect. When you click an upgrade offer linked from LinkedIn, the system now records your origin as a marketing source tag rather than a generic referral code, so future visits can carry that same source. Both changes are live today for visitors who reach the payment flow through the LinkedIn tracking link and complete checkout.

ai.title: Add UTM source tracking to Stripe payment success URL
ai.summary: UTM source parameters are now appended to the Stripe checkout success URL in web/src/lib/stripe.ts. The implementation extracts utm_source from the query string (stripping the first 12 characters) and adds it to the successUrl object before redirection. This change enables attribution tracking for payment completions originating from specific marketing campaigns.

eli5.text: When someone completes a payment through the new checkout flow, the system now includes in the confirmation page's address the information about which marketing source brought them there. You would notice this as part of the longer web address you briefly see in your browser after paying if you came from a specific campaign link, but it doesn't change anything visible on the payment success screen itself. This only applies to the latest checkout process that routes users to the dedicated confirmation page.

ai.title: Refactor payment tracking and success flow
ai.summary: Payment tracking refactored in `web/src/lib/linkedin.ts` and `web/src/lib/stripe.ts`. `trackUpgradeClick` now returns `URLSearchParams` instead of a string query fragment. `stripe.ts` updates `redirectToCheckout` to use Stripe's `{CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}` placeholder in `successUrl` and removes manual UTM parameter appending to the checkout session API call.

eli5.text: When someone upgrades and comes from LinkedIn, the system now passes along their LinkedIn tracking ID automatically through Stripe's checkout, so the payment success page can record the conversion without the old manual URL building. The tracking code for LinkedIn is currently switched off (commented out), so while the new handoff is in place it won't actually fire yet. You wouldn't notice anything right now, but the plumbing is ready for when LinkedIn tracking is turned back on.

ai.title: Add payment-success page tracking LinkedIn conversions
ai.summary: New `payment-success` page fires `trackUpgradeClick` on mount to confirm LinkedIn conversions. `stripe.ts` removes pre-checkout tracking and utm param injection, relying on the success page instead. `linkedin.ts` renamed to `trackConversions.ts` with active `linkedInTrack` call and `li_fat_id` cleanup. Covers Web surface.

eli5.text: When you finish a Codebuff Pro payment, LinkedIn can now properly record that a sale came from its ad. Previously the tracking was set up on the checkout button itself and relied on passing along an ID through several links; now that ID is carried through the payment flow and the actual LinkedIn notification happens once you land on the payment-success page (the "Payment successful!" screen with the credits image). This only affects visitors who arrived at Codebuff via a LinkedIn ad and then upgraded to Pro, they get counted as a conversion. It is live today for anyone using the web app.

ai.title: Fix Stripe checkout success URL
ai.summary: Stripe checkout success_url redirects to /payment-success instead of /pricing. payment-success page shows CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS.PAID. Removed duplicate successUrl from redirectToCheckout call. Files: web/src/app/api/stripe/checkout-session/route.ts, web/src/app/payment-success/page.tsx, web/src/lib/stripe.ts.

eli5.text: After you finish paying for CodeBuff Pro through Stripe, you now land on a dedicated 'Payment successful' page instead of being sent back to the pricing page. That page now tells you exactly how many credits you have available, using the same number shown across the rest of the app, rather than a generic welcome message. The redirect URL set up during checkout was pointing to the old destination, so it has been corrected to match the new page, and a leftover, duplicate success address that was being sent in two places has been removed. The change is live in the code that runs today, so anyone who subscribes through Stripe will see the updated page.
